sop_modules.name: Setup — Floor Protection, Countertop/Backsplash/Wall/Ceiling/Appliance Masking, Contents Verification, Hardware & Door/Drawer Removal
sop_modules.description: Full setup module for interior cabinet repaint. Floor protection (full kitchen for spray, perimeter for brush). Countertop and backsplash masking (CRITICAL high-value surfaces — always present in RP). Wall and ceiling masking for spray. Appliance protection (ALWAYS in RP — appliances always present in occupied homes). Plumbing/electrical masking. Cabinet contents verification (homeowner empties, painter verifies). Hardware removal with paint scoring for painted-over RP hardware. Door/drawer removal and labeling.

tasks.name: Install full kitchen floor protection for spray
tasks.notes: DIRECT from NC TSK_CABT_PROTECT_FLOOR_FULL. RP always has finished floors — canvas drop cloths + tape edges.

tasks.name: Install perimeter floor protection for brush
tasks.notes: DIRECT from NC TSK_CABT_PROTECT_FLOOR_PERIM.

tasks.name: Protect countertop surfaces
tasks.notes: DIRECT from NC TSK_CABT_PROTECT_COUNTERTOP. CRITICAL: high-value surfaces (granite, quartz, marble). Always present in RP.

tasks.name: Mask backsplash
tasks.notes: DIRECT from NC TSK_CABT_PROTECT_BACKSPLASH. Always present in RP kitchen.

tasks.name: Mask walls for spray overspray
tasks.notes: DIRECT from NC TSK_CABT_PROTECT_WALL. In RP, walls are ALWAYS finished — masking is mandatory for spray.

tasks.name: Mask ceiling for spray overspray
tasks.notes: DIRECT from NC TSK_CABT_PROTECT_CEILING.

tasks.name: Mask and protect appliances
tasks.notes: MODIFIED from NC: was conditional/atypical in NC. In RP, appliance protection is ALWAYS required — appliances are always present in occupied homes. Full wrap for spray, paper/tape for brush.

tasks.name: Mask sink plumbing in base cabinet
tasks.notes: DIRECT from NC TSK_CABT_PROTECT_PLUMBING.

tasks.name: Remove switch plates and mask electrical
tasks.notes: DIRECT from NC TSK_CABT_PROTECT_ELECTRICAL.

tasks.name: Verify all cabinet contents removed by homeowner
tasks.notes: RP-NEW. Walk all cabinets to verify homeowner has emptied contents. Check uppers, lowers, drawers, pantry. Any remaining items must be removed and staged before painting can begin.

tasks.name: Score paint, remove all cabinet hardware, bag, label
tasks.notes: MODIFIED from NC TSK_CABT_REMOVE_HARDWARE. RP hardware is often painted over — score paint around hinge barrels and screw heads before removal. ~30-50% slower than NC. May require screw extractor for stripped painted-over screws.

tasks.name: Remove cabinet doors and label
tasks.notes: DIRECT from NC TSK_CABT_REMOVE_DOORS. Removal technique identical once hardware is removed.

tasks.name: Remove cabinet drawers and label
tasks.notes: DIRECT from NC TSK_CABT_REMOVE_DRAWERS.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Floor protection > Countertop/backsplash masking > Wall/ceiling masking (spray) > Appliance masking > Plumbing/electrical masking > Contents verification > Hardware removal (score first in RP) > Door/drawer removal and labeling. All setup complete before assessment begins.

sop_modules.name: Condition Assessment — Visual Inspect, Adhesion Test, Coating ID, Factory Finish Type, Moisture Check, Thermofoil Gate, Lead Screen
sop_modules.description: RP-SPECIFIC assessment module — 100% RP_NEW. No NC equivalent. Systematic assessment of all cabinet components (frames, doors, drawers, interiors if in scope). Condition inspection maps defects per component type. Adhesion test (ASTM D3359 cross-hatch) is CRITICAL for cabinets due to diverse existing finish types. Coating identification via solvent test determines existing finish type (lacquer, oil, latex, thermofoil, catalyzed varnish) for primer routing. Moisture check on base cabinets and bath vanity. Thermofoil go/no-go gate if vinyl-wrapped doors present. Lead screening conditional on pre-1978 homes. All tasks are FIXED time. Assessment results drive downstream task activation: primer selection, prep intensity, contamination treatment.

tasks.name: Visual condition inspection — all cabinet components
tasks.description: Systematic visual inspection of all cabinet surfaces: frames, doors, drawers, interiors (if in scope). Document condition per component — doors may be GOOD while frames are FAIR. Photograph defects. Map damage areas on cabinet layout diagram. Assign condition_scale (GOOD/FAIR/POOR) based on worst-condition component.

quality_notes.QT3: Standard visual scan with work light, document visible defects per component type
quality_notes.QT4: Systematic scan with raking light, photograph all defect areas, per-component condition mapping
quality_notes.QT5: Exhaustive assessment, multiple passes, raking light, full photographic documentation per component, cross-light surface defect scan

tasks.notes: RP-NEW. 20-40 min per room depending on QT.

tasks.name: Adhesion test — ASTM D3359 cross-hatch tape test
tasks.description: Cross-hatch tape test on representative cabinet sections. Test minimum 3 locations per room: one upper door, one lower door, one frame section. CRITICAL for cabinets due to diverse existing finish types — factory lacquer, thermofoil, oil-based enamel all have distinct adhesion characteristics. Adhesion failure triggers full adhesion/bonding primer workflow.

quality_notes.all: Test at minimum 3 locations per room (1 upper door, 1 lower door, 1 frame). Record pass/fail per ASTM D3359 classification.

tasks.notes: RP-NEW. 10-15 min per room. CRITICAL assessment for cabinets.

tasks.name: Coating identification — solvent test for existing finish type
tasks.description: Chemical solvent test to identify existing coating: mineral spirits dissolves alkyd, xylene softens lacquer, denatured alcohol dissolves shellac, acetone softens latex. Test in inconspicuous location (inside door edge, inside frame). Results drive primer routing — factory lacquer requires bonding primer, oil-based requires adhesion primer, latex over latex may skip prime. Cabinet coating ID is more complex than any other interior RP surface (5 possible finish types vs 2 for doors/trim).

quality_notes.all: Test at minimum 2 locations per room. Document result: painted_latex, painted_oil, lacquer, catalyzed_varnish, thermofoil, or unknown.

tasks.notes: RP-NEW. 10-15 min per room. Cabinet-specific — not shared with other RP specs.

tasks.name: Moisture check — base cabinets and bath vanity
tasks.description: Moisture meter reading on base cabinet floor, back wall, and sides. Check under-sink area for active leaks. Check dishwasher-adjacent cabinet. For bath vanity: check all interior surfaces. If moisture detected above threshold, GATE: resolve source before painting. Active moisture is a STOP WORK condition.

quality_notes.all: Moisture meter reading at all base cabinet locations. Flag active moisture for remediation by other trades.

tasks.notes: RP-NEW. 5-10 min per room.

tasks.name: Thermofoil assessment gate — paintability determination
tasks.description: If thermofoil cabinets detected: inspect all door/drawer edges, corners, and heat-exposed areas (near oven, dishwasher) for vinyl lifting, bubbling, or delamination. ANY delamination = not paintable — recommend replacement. Intact thermofoil passes gate for painting with bonding primer. GO/NO-GO decision document.

quality_notes.all: Inspect all edges, corners, heat-exposed areas. GO/NO-GO decision documented with photos.

tasks.notes: RP-NEW. 10-15 min per room. Conditional on thermofoil presence. Cabinet-specific gate.

tasks.name: Lead paint screening — pre-1978 homes
tasks.description: XRF or swab test for lead paint on cabinet surfaces. Cabinets are HIGH RISK for lead paint — oil-based enamel with lead pigment was standard on kitchen cabinetry through the 1970s. If positive, triggers MOD_RRP_INT_CONTAINMENT shared module for all subsequent prep work.

quality_notes.all: Test at minimum 2 locations per room (1 door, 1 frame). Document result. If positive, activate RRP containment.

tasks.notes: RP-NEW. 10-15 min per room. Conditional on pre-1978 home.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Condition inspection first > Adhesion test at representative sections > Coating ID (solvent test) > Moisture check (base cabinets/vanity) > Thermofoil gate (if applicable) > Lead screen (if pre-1978). Assessment results determine which prep, prime, and treatment tasks activate downstream.

sop_modules.name: Lead-Safe RRP Containment (Shared Module)
sop_modules.description: Shared lead-safe work practice module for all interior RP specs. Conditional on home built before 1978 AND positive lead test. Cabinets are HIGH RISK for lead paint — oil-based enamel with lead pigment was standard on kitchen cabinetry through the 1970s. This module is NOT owned by this spec — it is a shared module referenced by all interior RP specs. Per EPA RRP Rule 40 CFR 745.

tasks.name: Lead Test (XRF or Swab)
tasks.notes: Test at minimum 1 door + 1 frame location per room. Cabinets are high-risk — often last surfaces to transition from oil to latex.

tasks.name: RRP Containment Setup
tasks.notes: Poly sheeting on floors and openings, warning signs at entry points, restrict entry to certified personnel. Per EPA RRP Rule 40 CFR 745.

tasks.name: HEPA Vacuum After Paint Disturbance
tasks.notes: HEPA vacuum all surfaces after each sanding/scraping disturbance to capture lead-contaminated dust.

tasks.name: RRP Containment Removal and Visual Clearance
tasks.notes: Remove containment, visual clearance inspection. No visible dust or debris.

tasks.name: Lead-Contaminated Waste Disposal
tasks.notes: Package and dispose of lead-contaminated debris per EPA RRP Rule.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Lead test first > If positive: containment setup > All prep tasks use wet methods > HEPA vacuum after each disturbance > Containment removal after all prep complete > Waste disposal.

sop_modules.name: Surface Preparation — Grease Wash, Degloss (4 Item Types), Chemical Degloss, Scrape/Feather, Damage Repair, Caulk Assess/Replace, Mildew/Smoke Treatment, Vacuum
sop_modules.description: Condition-driven prep module for cabinet RP. GOOD condition: grease wash + degloss + dust wipe. FAIR condition: add scrape/feather, caulk assess/replace, damage repair. POOR condition: full scrape, extensive feathering, contamination treatment, comprehensive repair. Degloss replaces NC sand tasks — existing semi-gloss/gloss finish requires degloss rather than bare-wood sanding. Fill tasks from NC are NOT_APPLICABLE (already filled) — replaced with condition-driven damage repair. Caulk is MODIFIED from NC full caulk to assess-and-replace. Prep pool modifiers: condition_scale x door_style x height (frame tasks) x kitchen_complexity (frame/protection tasks).

tasks.name: TSP/degreaser wash — kitchen grease removal
tasks.description: Full TSP substitute or kitchen degreaser wash on all paintable surfaces. Work top-down. Multiple passes may be needed above range and near cooktop. Verify clean with white cloth test. MANDATORY for all kitchen cabinet RP. Bath vanity: lighter wash (soap scum, not grease). Replaces NC TSK_CABT_DUST_CLEAN.
tasks.notes: MODIFIED from NC TSK_CABT_DUST_CLEAN. NC: 25 min construction dust wipe. RP: 35-45 min TSP/degreaser wash (condition-dependent). Fundamentally different cleaning scope.

tasks.name: Degloss face frames and box surfaces
tasks.description: Mechanical degloss (120-150 grit for lacquer, 180-220 grit for latex) on all face frame surfaces — stiles, rails, end panels, toe kicks, filler strips. Existing semi-gloss/gloss finish requires aggressive degloss for primer/paint adhesion. Chemical degloss option for complex profile areas. Replaces NC TSK_CABT_SAND_FRAMES.

quality_notes.QT3: Thorough degloss — mechanical or chemical, all accessible frame surfaces
quality_notes.QT4: Full degloss with adhesion verification, profile details addressed
quality_notes.QT5: Complete degloss with verification and spot adhesion re-test

tasks.notes: MODIFIED from NC TSK_CABT_SAND_FRAMES. NC QT3: 175 SF/hr bare wood sand. RP QT3: ~130-150 SF/hr (harder existing finish, 120-150 grit for lacquer).

tasks.name: Degloss cabinet doors
tasks.description: Mechanical degloss on cabinet door faces. Rate varies by door_style — slab fastest, raised_panel slowest (recessed areas trap existing finish). Chemical deglosser may be needed for raised_panel/shaker profiles where sandpaper cannot reach. Doors on sawhorses. Replaces NC TSK_CABT_SAND_DOORS.

quality_notes.QT3: Thorough degloss — mechanical or chemical, full face
quality_notes.QT4: Full degloss with adhesion verification, panel recesses addressed
quality_notes.QT5: Complete degloss with verification, all panel detail areas addressed

tasks.notes: MODIFIED from NC TSK_CABT_SAND_DOORS. NC QT3: 18 EA/hr. RP QT3: ~12-15 EA/hr. door_style modifier applies.

tasks.name: Degloss cabinet drawer fronts
tasks.description: Mechanical degloss on drawer front faces. Same technique as doors but ~0.7x door time per unit (smaller surface). Drawers on sawhorses. Replaces NC TSK_CABT_SAND_DRAWERS.
tasks.notes: MODIFIED from NC TSK_CABT_SAND_DRAWERS. NC QT3: 24 EA/hr. RP QT3: ~16-20 EA/hr. door_style modifier applies.

tasks.name: Degloss cabinet interior surfaces
tasks.description: Light scuff degloss on cabinet interior surfaces. Always QT3 effort level regardless of exterior tier. Interior surfaces less exposed to wear/contamination — light 220-grit scuff typically sufficient. Spray-accessible interiors.
tasks.notes: RP-NEW (NC had no degloss for interiors — bare wood sand only). Always QT3. ~175-200 SF/hr.

tasks.name: Chemical degloss — liquid sander for profiled doors/drawers
tasks.description: Apply liquid sander/deglosser (Wilbond, Krud Kutter Gloss-Off) to profiled door and drawer faces where mechanical sanding cannot reach all surfaces. Raised panel recesses and shaker inside corners. Wipe on, allow dwell time, wipe off. NOT applicable to thermofoil (solvents damage vinyl). Supplemental to mechanical degloss — used on profile areas only.
tasks.notes: RP-NEW. ~8-12 EA/hr. NOT for thermofoil — solvents damage vinyl wrap.

tasks.name: Scrape loose/failing paint to sound substrate
tasks.description: Scrape all loose, cracking, and delaminating paint from cabinet surfaces (frames, doors, drawers as affected). Work carefully on profiled doors to avoid gouging substrate. Frame joints and edge detail areas are primary failure locations. Collect and contain scrape debris (HEPA vacuum if RRP active).
tasks.notes: RP-NEW. 20-60 min per room (condition-dependent).

tasks.name: Feather-sand scrape edges for smooth transition
tasks.description: Feather-sand all scrape edges to create smooth transition between scraped areas and sound paint. Non-negotiable at all tiers — cabinet finishes are scrutinized at arm's length. Use 150-180 grit. Profile areas require flexible sanding approach. Ridge telegraphing through semi-gloss/gloss cabinet finishes is unacceptable.
tasks.notes: RP-NEW. 15-40 min per room. Non-negotiable at all tiers.

tasks.name: Repair surface damage — dings, scratches, impact damage
tasks.description: Fill and repair surface damage on cabinet surfaces: dings, scratches, impact marks, hardware relocation holes. Different from NC fill (which addresses bare wood fastener holes). RP damage repair uses lightweight spackle or wood filler depending on damage depth. Includes sand-flush after fill.

quality_notes.QT3: Fill obvious damage and hardware change holes
quality_notes.QT4: Fill all visible defects, careful feathering

tasks.notes: RP-NEW. Replaces NC TSK_CABT_FILL_FRAMES/DOORS/DRAWERS (NOT_APPLICABLE in RP). 10-30 min per room.

tasks.name: Sand filled/repaired areas smooth
tasks.description: Sand all filler spots and damage repair areas flush with surrounding surface. Use contour sanding for profile areas on profiled doors. Must be invisible under primer.
tasks.notes: DIRECT from NC TSK_CABT_SAND_FILL. Sanding technique identical whether NC or RP fill.

tasks.name: Assess and replace failed caulk — cabinet-to-wall joints
tasks.description: Inspect all existing caulk at cabinet-to-wall joints. Remove and replace cracked, shrunk, separated, or mildewed sections. RP assesses existing caulk and replaces only failed sections (15-30% typical). Modified from NC TSK_CABT_CAULK_JOINTS (which applies new caulk to all bare joints).

quality_notes.QT3: Replace visibly failed sections — cracked or separated joints
quality_notes.QT4: Comprehensive assessment, replace all suspect and failed joints
quality_notes.QT5: Critical assessment, replace all joints not in perfect condition, perfect tooled bead

tasks.notes: MODIFIED from NC TSK_CABT_CAULK_JOINTS. NC QT3: 80 LF/hr (full caulk). RP QT3: ~100-120 LF/hr (walk-and-assess, replace 15-30%).

tasks.name: Biocide treatment for mildew/mold — under-sink and bath vanity
tasks.description: Apply mildew/mold biocide treatment to affected cabinet surfaces. Common under-sink and bath vanity locations. Allow dwell time per product instructions. Rinse or wipe per product requirements. Source must be resolved BEFORE treatment (gate from assessment).
tasks.notes: RP-NEW. 15-25 min per room. Conditional on moisture damage + mildew.

tasks.name: Smoke/nicotine pre-treatment wash
tasks.description: Heavy TSP wash to remove surface nicotine/smoke film before shellac stain blocker application. Kitchen cabinets near stove may have combined grease + smoke contamination. May require multiple passes.
tasks.notes: RP-NEW. 20-35 min per room.

tasks.name: Vacuum floor after prep work
tasks.notes: DIRECT from NC TSK_CABT_VACUUM_FLOOR. Post-sanding/scraping vacuum identical.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Grease wash (MANDATORY) > Degloss all item types (mechanical + chemical for profiles) > Scrape loose paint (FAIR/POOR) > Feather edges (FAIR/POOR) > Damage repair (FAIR/POOR) > Sand fill > Caulk assess/replace > Mildew treatment (conditional) > Smoke treatment (conditional) > Vacuum floor.

sop_modules.name: Primer Application — State-Driven + Factory-Finish-Type-Driven Primer Selection
sop_modules.description: State-driven + factory-finish-type-driven primer application. 4 RP primer systems: SYS_PRIMER_ADHESION_INT (painted_oil, failing, peeling conditions), SYS_PRIMER_BONDING_FACTORY (factory lacquer, catalyzed varnish, thermofoil), SYS_PRIMER_STAINBLOCK_INT (smoke damage — shellac BIN), SYS_PRIMER_MILDEW_INT (moisture damage with mildew). GOOD condition with sound latex may skip prime entirely. Spray/brush variants for each item type. Includes post-primer adhesion test (quality gate for bonding primer — verify it is working before proceeding to finish coats). NC had substrate-driven primer (SS_BARE); RP has condition + factory-finish routing.

applies_when.notes: Conditional on condition_scale + factory_finish_type. GOOD condition with painted_latex and passing adhesion test may skip entire prime module. All other combinations require priming.

tasks.name: Spray primer on face frames and box surfaces
tasks.notes: MODIFIED from NC TSK_CABT_PRIME_FRAMES. Application technique identical. Primer chemistry changed: state-driven + factory-finish-type-driven routing replaces NC substrate-driven routing. Rates ~same.

tasks.name: Brush primer on face frames and box surfaces
tasks.notes: RP splits prime into spray/brush variants (NC had single prime task). Roll and Tip technique per FFD SS15.6.

tasks.name: Spray primer on cabinet doors (flat on sawhorses)
tasks.notes: MODIFIED from NC TSK_CABT_PRIME_DOORS. State-driven primer routing. Rates ~same.

tasks.name: Brush primer on cabinet doors (flat on sawhorses)
tasks.notes: RP splits prime into spray/brush variants. Roll and Tip technique.

tasks.name: Spray primer on drawer fronts (flat on sawhorses)
tasks.notes: MODIFIED from NC TSK_CABT_PRIME_DRAWERS. State-driven primer routing. Rates ~same.

tasks.name: Brush primer on drawer fronts (flat on sawhorses)
tasks.notes: RP splits prime into spray/brush variants.

tasks.name: Spray primer on cabinet interiors
tasks.notes: MODIFIED from NC TSK_CABT_PRIME_INTERIOR. Spray-only for interiors. Interior condition assessed separately — may be GOOD while exterior is FAIR/POOR. Always QT3.

tasks.name: Post-primer adhesion test — verify bonding
tasks.description: After primer application, verify adhesion with tape test on representative sections. CRITICAL when bonding primer used on factory lacquer/thermofoil — if bonding primer fails adhesion test, STOP and evaluate alternative primers or stripping. Quality gate that does not exist in NC (bare substrates always accept primer).

quality_notes.all: Tape test at minimum 2 primed locations per room. Pass/fail documented. Failure = STOP WORK.

tasks.notes: RP-NEW. 10-15 min per room. Quality gate for bonding/adhesion primers.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Prime frames (spray or brush) > Prime doors (spray or brush) > Prime drawers (spray or brush) > Prime interiors (spray-only, if in scope) > Post-primer adhesion test (quality gate). Primer chemistry determined by assessment results: condition_scale + factory_finish_type routing.

sop_modules.name: Between-Coat Interstage — Inspect, Sand, Patch, Spot Coat, Tack
sop_modules.description: Fine-finish interstage protocol. Runs AFTER each coat EXCEPT the final coat. Identical to NC interstage in technique — once coating is applied, interstage work is product-driven not substrate-driven. QT-scaled sanding discipline: QT3 spot sand nibs 220 grit, QT4 full light sand 220 grit, QT5 thorough full sand 220-320 grit. Separate tasks for frames (SF), doors (EA), drawers (EA), interior (SF). Universal for cabinets — scrutinized fine-finish surface.
sop_modules.run_rule: Runs AFTER each coat EXCEPT the final coat

tasks.name: Clean work area between coats
tasks.notes: DIRECT from NC TSK_CABT_CLEAN_AREA.

tasks.name: Inspect previous coat for defects

quality_notes.QT3: Quick scan at 6 ft — runs, sags, holidays
quality_notes.QT4: Systematic scan at 3 ft with work light — all visible defects, sheen uniformity
quality_notes.QT5: Critical inspection at arm's length under raking light — zero tolerance

tasks.notes: DIRECT from NC TSK_CABT_INSPECT_COAT.

tasks.name: Sand between coats on frames

quality_notes.QT4: Full light sand entire surface — 220 grit uniform scratch
quality_notes.QT5: Thorough full sand — 220-320 grit, every imperfection

tasks.notes: DIRECT from NC TSK_CABT_SAND_BETWEEN_FRAMES.

tasks.name: Sand between coats on doors
tasks.notes: DIRECT from NC TSK_CABT_SAND_BETWEEN_DOORS.

tasks.name: Sand between coats on drawers
tasks.notes: DIRECT from NC TSK_CABT_SAND_BETWEEN_DRAWERS.

tasks.name: Sand between coats on interiors
tasks.notes: DIRECT from NC TSK_CABT_SAND_BETWEEN_INTERIOR. Always QT3.

tasks.name: Patch and repair interstage defects
tasks.notes: DIRECT from NC TSK_CABT_PATCH_DEFECTS.

tasks.name: Spot coat patched areas
tasks.notes: DIRECT from NC TSK_CABT_SPOT_COAT.

tasks.name: Tack cloth all surfaces before next coat
tasks.notes: DIRECT from NC TSK_CABT_TACK_CLEAN.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Clean area > Inspect coat > Sand between (frames SF, doors EA, drawers EA, interior SF) > Patch defects > Spot coat patches > Tack clean. Repeat between each coat pair.

sop_modules.name: Finish Coat Application — Spray or Brush, All Item Types
sop_modules.description: Finish coat application — spray or brush. DIRECT transfer from NC in technique — once surface is prepped, deglossed, and primed, finish coat application is identical between NC and RP. Frame tasks (SF) + door tasks (EA) + drawer tasks (EA) + interior tasks (SF, spray-only). 2 coats standard (QT3-QT4), 3 coats QT5 brush per FFD 15.10.3. Fine-finish coating systems: SYS_FF_STANDARD_ACRYLIC (QT3), SYS_FF_MODIFIED_URETHANE (QT4), SYS_FF_PREMIUM (QT5). Interstage runs between each coat pair.

tasks.name: Spray finish coat on frames
tasks.notes: DIRECT from NC TSK_CABT_SPRAY_FRAMES. Rates identical.

tasks.name: Brush finish coat on frames (Roll and Tip)
tasks.notes: DIRECT from NC TSK_CABT_BRUSH_FRAMES. Roll and Tip technique per FFD SS15.6.

tasks.name: Spray finish coat on doors
tasks.notes: DIRECT from NC TSK_CABT_SPRAY_DOORS. Rates identical.

tasks.name: Brush finish coat on doors (Roll and Tip)
tasks.notes: DIRECT from NC TSK_CABT_BRUSH_DOORS. Lead skill for brush on doors — close viewing distance.

tasks.name: Spray finish coat on drawer fronts
tasks.notes: DIRECT from NC TSK_CABT_SPRAY_DRAWERS.

tasks.name: Brush finish coat on drawer fronts (Roll and Tip)
tasks.notes: DIRECT from NC TSK_CABT_BRUSH_DRAWERS.

tasks.name: Spray finish coat on interiors
tasks.notes: DIRECT from NC TSK_CABT_SPRAY_INTERIOR. Always QT3 regardless of exterior tier. Spray-only.

tasks.name: Final quality inspection per tier

quality_notes.QT3: Quick scan at 6 ft, ambient light — obvious defects only
quality_notes.QT4: Systematic scan at 3 ft with work light — all visible defects, sheen uniformity
quality_notes.QT5: Critical inspection at arm's length under raking light — zero tolerance, every door and drawer

tasks.notes: DIRECT from NC TSK_CABT_FINAL_INSPECT.

tasks.name: Touch-up defects from final inspection
tasks.notes: DIRECT from NC TSK_CABT_TOUCHUP.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Finish coat 1 (all items) > Interstage > Finish coat 2 (all items) > [QT5 brush: Interstage > Finish coat 3] > Final inspect > Touch-up.

sop_modules.name: Cure, Reassembly, Protection Teardown, Contents Replacement, Customer Walkthrough
sop_modules.description: Final phase: cure period (5-7 day minimum, SEPARATE MOBILIZATION), then reassembly and cleanup. Door/drawer reinstallation with alignment check. Hardware reinstallation (may need hinge mortise cleaning for paint build-up from multiple repaint cycles). Post-reinstall touch-up. Protection teardown across all zones. Contents replacement coordination with homeowner. Customer walkthrough with per-door/drawer inspection — RP-specific. Final vacuum and tool cleanup.
sop_modules.notes: 5-7 day cure period (minimum), then reassembly. SEPARATE MOBILIZATION — Visit 2. 7-14 days for waterborne alkyd at QT4.

tasks.name: Cure period — doors stored safely
tasks.notes: DIRECT from NC TSK_CABT_CURE_PERIOD. MANDATORY 5-7 day minimum. 7-14 days for waterborne alkyd. Product-driven, not substrate-driven.

tasks.name: Reinstall doors, verify alignment and operation
tasks.notes: DIRECT from NC TSK_CABT_REINSTALL_DOORS. RP may need hinge mortise cleaning for paint build-up from multiple repaint cycles. Verify soft-close operation.

tasks.name: Reinstall drawers, check slides and operation
tasks.notes: DIRECT from NC TSK_CABT_REINSTALL_DRAWERS. Check slide operation, soft-close function.

tasks.name: Reinstall all cabinet hardware
tasks.notes: DIRECT from NC TSK_CABT_REINSTALL_HARDWARE. RP: clean paint from screw holes and hinge mortises. Account for paint build-up thickness — may need deeper mortise.

tasks.name: Adjust hinge alignment after reinstall
tasks.description: Fine-tune door alignment after reinstallation. Paint film thickness changes hinge geometry slightly. Check door-to-frame reveal uniformity. Adjust Euro hinge screws or shim traditional hinges. More critical in RP than NC due to accumulated paint thickness from multiple repaint cycles.
tasks.notes: RP-NEW. Paint build-up from multiple repaint cycles requires alignment verification.

tasks.name: Touch-up after reinstallation
tasks.notes: DIRECT from NC TSK_CABT_REINSTALL_TOUCHUP. Touch-up handling marks, hinge area nicks from reinstallation.

tasks.name: Coordinate cabinet contents replacement with homeowner
tasks.description: After final inspection and cure period, coordinate with homeowner for contents replacement. Painter does NOT replace contents (homeowner responsibility) but verifies cabinets are clean, dry, and ready for use. Advise homeowner to wait 24-48 hrs before heavy loading.
tasks.notes: RP-NEW. 5-10 min per room.

tasks.name: Customer walkthrough and completion review
tasks.description: Post-completion walk-through with homeowner. Inspect every door and drawer face. Demonstrate door/drawer operation — alignment, soft-close function. Identify any touch-up needs. Confirm completion and customer satisfaction. Leave touch-up paint for homeowner.
tasks.notes: RP-NEW. 10-20 min per room. Cabinet walkthrough is more thorough than wall/trim — homeowner inspects every door and drawer individually.

tasks.name: Remove countertop protection
tasks.notes: DIRECT from NC TSK_CABT_REMOVE_COUNTERTOP_PROTECT.

tasks.name: Remove backsplash masking
tasks.notes: DIRECT from NC TSK_CABT_REMOVE_BACKSPLASH_MASK.

tasks.name: Remove wall masking
tasks.notes: DIRECT from NC TSK_CABT_REMOVE_WALL_MASK.

tasks.name: Remove ceiling masking
tasks.notes: DIRECT from NC TSK_CABT_REMOVE_CEILING_MASK.

tasks.name: Remove appliance protection
tasks.notes: DIRECT from NC TSK_CABT_REMOVE_APPLIANCE_MASK.

tasks.name: Remove floor protection
tasks.notes: DIRECT from NC TSK_CABT_REMOVE_FLOOR_PROTECT.

tasks.name: Final vacuum of work area
tasks.notes: DIRECT from NC TSK_CABT_VACUUM_FINAL.

tasks.notes: DIRECT from NC TSK_CABT_TOOL_CLEANUP.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Cure period (5-7 day minimum, SEPARATE MOBILIZATION) > Door reinstall > Drawer reinstall > Hardware reinstall > Hinge adjustment > Post-reinstall touch-up > Contents replacement coordination > Customer walkthrough > Protection teardown (countertop > backsplash > wall > ceiling > appliance > floor) > Final vacuum > Tool cleanup.

round_configurations.name: State-driven prime + 2 finish coats
round_configurations.description: Standard RP sequence for FAIR/POOR condition cabinets or factory lacquer/thermofoil/oil substrates requiring primer.
round_configurations.notes: Most common RP round. Prime coat is state-driven + factory-finish-type-driven (adhesion, bonding, stain-block, or mildew primer). Also applies to GOOD condition with painted_oil or factory lacquer/thermofoil (primer always required for these finishes regardless of condition).

round_configurations.name: 2 finish coats (no prime)
round_configurations.description: GOOD condition, no prime needed — sound latex paint with adhesion verified.
round_configurations.notes: Simplest and fastest RP round — cosmetic color change on sound latex. Skip prime when: adhesion test passes, existing paint is sound, existing coating is field-applied latex (not oil, not factory lacquer/thermofoil).

round_configurations.name: Prime + 3 finish coats (QT5 brush)
round_configurations.description: Maximum coat sequence. State-driven prime + 3 brush finish coats per FFD 15.10.3.
round_configurations.notes: QT5 brush adds 3rd finish coat per FFD 15.10.3 on top of state-driven primer. 4 total coats, 3 interstage cycles. Thorough 220-320 grit interstage.

round_configurations.name: 3 finish coats (QT5 brush, no prime)
round_configurations.description: QT5 + brush + GOOD condition with latex existing.
round_configurations.notes: QT5 brush adds 3rd finish coat per FFD 15.10.3 even without prime. 3 total coats, 2 interstage cycles.

protection_metadata.notes: 10 protection zones (NC had 9 — RP adds contents_staging). Appliance_covers changed from conditional to always_in_rp. Highest protection zone count of any interior RP spec.

task_count_summary.notes: 80 tasks across 8 modules (vs NC 58 tasks across 7 modules). 75 CBRP-prefixed tasks + 5 shared RRP tasks. Assessment module (6 tasks) is 100% RP_NEW. Key RP additions: +6 assessment tasks, +8 RP-new prep tasks (grease wash, degloss x5, chemical degloss, scrape, feather, damage repair, mildew/smoke treatment), +4 prime spray/brush split + adhesion test gate, +4 RP-new cleanup tasks (hinge adjust, contents replace, customer walkthrough). NC NOT_APPLICABLE tasks removed: 3 fill tasks, 1 MDF edge seal, 1 dust clean (replaced by grease wash). 5 shared RRP tasks conditional on pre-1978 home. Within projected 68-78 range when excluding 5 conditional RRP tasks (75 CBRP tasks).
